parts.label: (a)(i)
key_concepts: SHM maximum speed at equilibrium position
gradient of displacement-time graph equals velocity
hints: Hint 1: Think about where on the $l$-$t$ graph the mass is at the middle of its swing ($l = 15\text{ cm}$) and whether the graph is sloping up or down there for downward motion.
parts.proper_answer: $t = 0.225\text{ s}$ and $t = 0.525\text{ s}$, where $l = 15\text{ cm}$ and $l$ is increasing.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Where is speed maximum in SHM**
In simple harmonic motion you move fastest as you rush through the equilibrium position, and you momentarily stop at the top and bottom turning points. Here the length swings between $13\text{ cm}$ and $17\text{ cm}$, so equilibrium is halfway at $$l_0 = \frac{17+13}{2} = 15\text{ cm}$$

Step 2: **Pick the downward direction**
$l$ is the length of the spring measured down from the support. So a longer $l$ means the mass is lower down. Moving downwards means $l$ is increasing, so you need the parts of the curve with positive gradient. Those are the rising sections centred on $t \approx 0.225\text{ s}$ and $t \approx 0.525\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Look at Fig. 4.2 and find the time for one complete repeat, for example from one peak at $l = 17\text{ cm}$ to the next peak.
Hint 2: Recall how angular frequency links to that repeat time for SHM and check your units give $\text{rad s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Read the period T from the graph**
One full oscillation is peak to peak or trough to trough. The peaks in $l$ are at $t = 0$, $0.30\text{ s}$ and $0.60\text{ s}$. So $$T = 0.30 - 0 = 0.30\text{ s}$$ You can check with the troughs at $0.15\text{ s}$ and $0.45\text{ s}$ which also give $0.30\text{ s}$.

Step 2: **Convert to angular frequency**
For SHM the phase advances by $2\pi$ radians per period: $$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T}$$ $$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{0.30} \approx 20.9\text{ rad s}^{-1} \approx 21\text{ rad s}^{-1}$$

parts.label: (a)(iii)
hints: Hint 1: Find the amplitude $x_0$ as the maximum distance from the $15\text{ cm}$ equilibrium line in Fig. 4.2, remembering to convert cm to m.
Hint 2: Think about which SHM speed formula gives the largest value and where it occurs, then combine it with your $\omega$ from (a)(ii).
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Get the amplitude**
Amplitude is the swing away from equilibrium, not peak to trough. $$x_0 = 17\text{ cm} - 15\text{ cm} = 2.0\text{ cm} = 2.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}$$ This is a common slip, so always halve the total $4.0\text{ cm}$ range.

Step 2: **Use v_max at x = 0**
In SHM $$v = \pm \omega \sqrt{x_0^2 - x^2}$$ so speed is largest when $x = 0$: $$v_{max} = \omega x_0$$ $$v_{max} = 20.94 \times 2.0 \times 10^{-2} \approx 0.42\text{ m s}^{-1}$$ This matches the value to be shown.

parts.label: (b)
key_concepts: intercepts v0 at x=0 and x0 at v=0
phase relationship between v and x
hints: Hint 1: Start by listing the two key numbers you already have: the maximum displacement from equilibrium and the maximum speed from (a)(iii).
Hint 2: Think about what the velocity must be when the mass is momentarily stopped at $x = \pm x_0$, and what it is when it shoots through $x = 0$.
Hint 3: Recall the overall shape of a $v$ against $x$ plot for undamped SHM and that it must be a smooth closed loop centred on the origin.
parts.proper_answer: Closed oval (ellipse) centred on $(0,0)$ passing through $(x,v) = (0, \pm 0.42\text{ m s}^{-1})$ and $(\pm 2.0\text{ cm}, 0)$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify the intercepts**
Let $x$ be displacement from equilibrium. From Fig. 4.2, $x$ goes from $-2.0\text{ cm}$ to $+2.0\text{ cm}$. From (a)(iii), $v$ goes from $-0.42\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $+0.42\text{ m s}^{-1}$. At the extremes the mass stops, so $v = 0$ when $x = \pm 2.0\text{ cm}$. At the centre it is fastest, so $|v| = 0.42\text{ m s}^{-1}$ when $x = 0$.

Step 2: **Draw the correct SHM shape**
Because $$v^2 = \omega^2(x_0^2 - x^2)$$ the $v$-$x$ graph is an ellipse, a smooth continuous oval surrounding the origin. Sketch it so it cuts the $v$-axis at $0.42$ and $-0.42$ and cuts the $x$-axis at $2.0$ and $-2.0$. Keep it symmetric in all four quadrants.
